column5: F: Someone changes the file somewhere else. | M: Open it again, and the page lists exactly what changed since the last stamp.

column5: F: What did that cell go through? | M: Its whole story: every value, who, and when. The name is typed, so it is not a signature.
column6: F: What did that cell go through? | M: Its whole story: every value, who, and when. The name is typed, so it is not a signature.

column5: F: Can I see the sheet as it was? | M: Pick any step. It comes back as it was, and you can download that version.
column6: F: Can I see the sheet as it was? | M: Pick any step. It comes back as it was, and you can download that version.

column5: F: Two people each changed a copy, and emailed them back. | M: Open the other copy. Different cells combine. The same cell changed two ways is a clash, with both values and both names. Nothing is overwritten until you choose.
column6: F: Two people each changed a copy, and emailed them back. | M: Open the other copy. Different cells combine. The same cell changed two ways is a clash, with both values and both names. Nothing is overwritten until you choose.

column5: M: Choose one, and finish. The merged file checks out, and that cell's story names both people.
column6: M: Choose one, and finish. The merged file checks out, and that cell's story names both people.

column5: F: And if someone edits the history by hand? | M: It is caught, and the entry is named. Stamp refuses to go on.
